analysis: Isoniazid is a medication primarily used for the treatment of tuberculosis. A well-documented side effect of isoniazid is its interference with the metabolism of vitamin B6 (pyridoxine). This occurs because isoniazid inhibits the enzyme pyridoxine kinase, which is essential for converting vitamin B6 into its active form. As a result, patients on isoniazid are at an increased risk of developing a vitamin B6 deficiency, which can lead to neurological symptoms due to impaired neurotransmitter synthesis. The evidence clearly supports that the deficiency most likely to be seen in patients on isoniazid is that of vitamin B6, not vitamins B12, B9, or B3, as there is no substantial evidence linking isoniazid with the metabolism of these other vitamins.
